title: Hellboy: The Board Game: The Review: The Video
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b_Obp5cBRZk

Daniel (@dungeondive) reviews Hellboy: The Board Game and hits an unusual snag — he adores it but struggles to recommend it, because the retail version is drastically thinner than the Kickstarter he backed (one enemy type and a handful of cards versus a huge roster). Designed by James Hewitt and Sophie Williams of Warhammer Quest: Silver Tower, it wears its comic-book roots proudly, down to the comic-sized rulebook Daniel keeps praising against Fireteam Zero's unwieldy tome. The heart is a random scenario generator — seven modular elements assembled from a Silver Tower-style "deck of doom" — that promises months of variety despite only eight set scenarios. Its standout mechanism is a colour-coded dice system where situations upgrade or downgrade your dice (red to black, yellow to nothing), plus a bonus blue die that can wreck your best roll; boss behaviour decks keep the big bads unpredictable, and an injury track lets heroes soak punishment before being knocked out. Three action cubes per hero, no fixed initiative, and a target-priority track round out a smooth, thematic experience. His conclusion: a fantastic game for backers, but retail buyers should brace to buy expansions to fill the gaps.

----

Does a huge Kickstarter-versus-retail gap sour you on a game, even a great one? And which board game best captures a comic or franchise you love?
